key_insight: Coupling large-eddy simulation with multi-grain-size sediment transport improves bed-deformation predictions and captures coarse–fine sediment sorting in meandering rivers.
engineering_relevance: Representing riverbed grain-size heterogeneity can improve scour and deposition assessments for flood management and infrastructure protection.
method: Couple large-eddy simulation with multi-grain-size sediment transport.
Track grain-size classes, local bed-load-layer fractions, and bed evolution.
Validate against flume measurements, then simulate large-scale meandering rivers.
evidence_signal: Against flume measurements, the multi-grain model reduced maximum scour-depth error from 37.98% to 3.83% and maximum deposition-height error from 48.35% to 11.54% compared with a uniform-sediment model.
watch_item: The abstract reports laboratory validation but no field-scale validation of the large-scale meandering-river predictions.
paper_title: Computational and experimental study of multi-grain-size sediment transport and sorting process
